prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a low-speed head-on collision claim. Injury: back strain. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1124; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened for a low-speed head-on collision reported by the insured driver. Vehicles came to rest in the travel lane with minor front-end damage reported on both units. Claimant reports neck and lower back discomfort at the scene and was evaluated by EMS, then released. Photos requested from the insured and the other driver's contact information obtained.

Entry 2: Spoke with the claimant by phone. Claimant reports a back strain and stiffness, with pain rated as moderate and worse in the morning. Claimant is not represented by an attorney and states they are handling the injury discussion directly. Explained the claims process, the documents needed, and the option to seek medical treatment. Asked for the treating provider's name and any imaging results.

Entry 3: Reviewed the police report, which lists the collision as a head-on impact at low speed with no citations issued. Both drivers gave consistent accounts of a lane drift by the other vehicle. Recorded the claimant's vehicle as drivable with bumper and hood damage. Appraisal scheduled at the next available location.

Entry 4: Received the claimant's medical records from the urgent care visit. Diagnosis is a lumbar strain with a recommendation for rest, over-the-counter pain relief, and a follow-up if symptoms persist beyond two weeks. No fractures or neurological findings noted. Sent a copy of the file summary to the medical review unit for documentation.

Entry 5: Claimant called to check on status. Advised that the injury evaluation is in progress and that the vehicle appraisal is complete. Explained that a settlement offer will follow once the medical review is finished. Reminded the claimant to keep receipts for any out-of-pocket treatment costs and to notify the office of any change in symptoms.
